Vrbovsko Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vrbovsko, Croatia

Not demolished. Vrbovsko, first mentioned in 1481 in Croatia's mountainous Gorski Kotar region, was depopulated under 16th-century Ottoman occupation before Serb settlers arrived from Bosnia and Dalmatia in 1599. Little is documented about its small Jewish community, which numbered only about 37 people across the wider area in 1931. Notably, two local residents, Antun and Katarina Šragalj, were recognized as Righteous Among the Nations in 2018 for saving a Jewish girl, Lea Gostl, during WWII. This cemetery's few surviving tombstones date from 1924 to 1932.
